punchline: In neighboring countries the share of people registered as organ donors ran from 12 percent to 99.98 percent, and the registration rule differed.
thirty_sec: In 2003 Eric Johnson and Daniel Goldstein compared European countries. In Germany, where people had to register to be donors, the effective consent rate was 12 percent. In Austria, where everyone counted as a donor unless they opted out, it was 99.98 percent. A Dutch donor register launched in 1998 with more than 12 million letters did not change its rate. Later researchers argue the true gap in donations is smaller.
